objective: Close the streak-policy/runtime mismatch by adding a bounded protected-interruption event that can neutralize streak liability without becoming a generic skip token, restoring rewards, or rewriting quest history.

roles_before.artifact: system-execution-streak:v1 breaks current streak on missed eligible days and protects earned progression, but has no persisted protected-interruption event.
system-pressure-profile:v1 and Challenge Contract v1 own bounded artificial pressure; misses forfeit prospective reward and can break streak.
PostgreSQL system_events is the mutable derived RPG/event owner with dedicated validated write paths.
system-controller.md schedules real execution windows and may create bounded Challenges under standing authorization.
streak-policy.mjs derives current/best/today status from immutable events.
app-v2.js renders streak states in the Status screen.
XP/owned Coins/skills/achievements/levels and verified history are irreversible.
Git plus immutable system_events preserve pre-change policy/runtime evidence.

role_dispositions.destination: Add streak.excused as a neutral protected-day event: it neither extends nor breaks current streak and cannot target future dates.
Challenge miss still expires parent and forfeits prospective reward. An excuse may protect streak history only; it never restores reward or terminal state.
Add migration 015 and PostgreSQL-only streak.excuse write path with bounded reason codes, idempotency and validation.
Allow deterministic follow-through only when current evidence establishes illness, safety risk, material external disruption, System failure or invalidated schedule; never ordinary avoidance.
Project EXCUSED_TODAY and preserve current streak across protected eligible days without incrementing it.
Render explicit Russian protected-day status while leaving all existing streak states intact.
No already-earned progression is touched by excuse semantics.
No historical event is edited; policy behavior is reconstructable from Git and append-only events.

capability_probes.assertion: An excused eligible day preserves current streak without incrementing it and projects EXCUSED_TODAY.
Excusing a Challenge-miss date may neutralize streak loss but cannot restore parent reward or rewrite EXPIRED lifecycle history.
PostgreSQL accepts only bounded streak.excuse reason codes, rejects future local dates, and replays idempotently.
Zero-credential/ephemeral runtime does not expose streak.excuse writes and continues to support existing read-only/dev behavior.
AT_RISK/SECURED/BROKEN/neutral streak states, Challenge admission, reminders, push and terminal-quest handling remain intact.
Shop, progression issuance, skills, achievements, focus, reminders and push owners are unaffected.
All pre-excuse behavior and player evidence remain recoverable from Git and immutable system_events.

tests.expected: protected interruption, Challenge interaction, terminal-reminder cancellation and original streak semantics PASS.
bounded reason validation, future-date rejection and idempotent PostgreSQL write PASS.
PostgreSQL HTTP smoke exposes and writes streak.excuse; ephemeral runtime remains fail-closed; model/docker regressions PASS.
EXCUSED_TODAY copy and existing player UI contract PASS.

known_intentional_losses: A protected eligible day no longer necessarily breaks current streak.
The controller may append a bounded streak.excused event when direct current evidence already establishes a protected interruption.

verification.candidate_readback: All candidate lanes passed after fixing the over-escaped streak.excused date regex and keeping the invalid-reason PostgreSQL test on the current local date. PostgreSQL smoke now exercises the streak.excuse HTTP write path; ephemeral runtime remains fail-closed.
verification.base_head_diff: Adds a bounded protected-interruption event/action, projection state, player copy, controller rule, PostgreSQL migration/store wrapper, HTTP smoke and regression coverage. It does not restore Challenge rewards, rewrite terminal quest history, alter earned progression, or create future-date skip tokens.
